metadata.title: TIMSS and PIRLS 2011 Relationships Report
metadata.venue: TIMSS & PIRLS International Study Center, Boston College

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The chapter uses TIMSS and PIRLS 2011 fourth-grade combined data across 34 countries and 3 benchmarking entities, with students nested within schools and countries. In the path-model estimation, the authors explicitly state that individual student case weights (HOUWGT) were used, and they also use Mplus “Complex” options with school as the cluster variable to correct standard errors for the clustered sampling design. The analyses also incorporate the TIMSS/PIRLS plausible values for the three achievement outcomes by running separate analyses for each PV and combining parameter estimates and standard errors. Because the study is not a machine-learning prediction pipeline, the weighting is applied for survey design representation rather than for ML model training.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: Plausible values are used for the three achievement outcomes (reading, mathematics, science) and the authors describe combining results across five PVs using Mplus facilities and constraints. However, the manuscript does not report a specific missing-data handling strategy for questionnaire or background variables (e.g., listwise deletion, multiple imputation, or other procedures). Given that the study relies on multiple questionnaire scales and latent-variable indicators, the missing-data approach is a reporting gap that prevents assessing potential bias from nonresponse.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The special TIMSS & PIRLS 2011 combined database includes only fourth-grade students assessed in all three subjects (reading, mathematics, science). The chapter 4 path-model analyses use the pooled dataset across 34 participating countries and 3 benchmarking entities (37 participants total) and estimate models with country as the between-level and students within country as the within-level. The authors report that the model is estimated using all five plausible values available for each achievement measure, and they use school as the cluster variable for complex-sample standard error correction. For country-by-country models, separate saturated path models are fitted for each participant; Ireland is noted as having missing data on some variables, implying that not all countries contribute equally to every country-specific path diagram.

data.outcome_summary: This report chapter analyzes relationships among home background factors and fourth-grade achievement in reading, mathematics, and science using TIMSS and PIRLS 2011 combined microdata. The analytic sample is restricted to students assessed in all three subjects in 34 countries plus 3 benchmarking entities (37 participants total), with achievement outcomes represented using five plausible values per domain. The authors estimate a two-level path model in Mplus with country as the between-level and students within country as the within-level, and they use Mplus “Complex” options with school as the cluster variable. Individual student case weights (HOUWGT) are applied, and parameter estimates are combined across plausible values using Mplus imputation/constraints. Results show that parental education and gender relate to achievement both directly and indirectly through home resources (books), home literacy/numeracy activities, and children’s early literacy/numeracy skills at school entry, with notable heterogeneity across countries and stronger gender mediation in reading than in mathematics/science.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This extraction is for an IEA/OECD-style large-scale assessment relationships report rather than an ML predictive paper. The chapter uses path modeling and multilevel estimation (not machine learning), so the schema’s ML technique fields are intentionally empty. The extraction also cannot populate per-country student counts because the provided text does not include a complete table of n_students by country; only the pooled N and qualitative country participation information are available.
